purpose: Document first-party local registry/map evidence and bounded anonymous geometry access review.
assessment: 201 valid, distinct Chief Surveyor-General Erven references verified in thirteen bounded cells around the unchanged ranked Klipgat WUP locator. The official DFFE-hosted service advertises GeoJSON but rejects that format in actual queries; explicit native Esri JSON queries succeed. A strict reader preserves every straight-ring coordinate and assigns native holes/components without repair; native curve representations and unsupported or ambiguous rings remain unavailable. Complete object-ID manifests, forced three-row paging (42 rows over fourteen pages), all 201 fresh native PRCL_KEY reads, explicit absence, footprint and source binding passed. Independent GEOS audit in EPSG:32735 found no invalid geometries, duplicates, sampled overlaps above 0.01 m² or operation errors. The sampled records all have publisher statuses R/C/E; no guessed lifecycle filter is applied. Citywide completeness, legal title, survey accuracy and broader identity uniqueness remain unverified.
registryAssessment: One official registered Erven feature covers the exact WUP point. This single exact-point result establishes local sample coverage only, not citywide completeness.

officialPrimarySources.observation: Chief Surveyor-General describes the national computerized spatial cadastral dataset of land parcels and rights.

Official Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment ArcGIS-hosted service identifies the national cadastral layer custodian as Chief Surveyor-General; layer 2 Erven is polygon geometry with query capability.
Moretele Local Municipality publishes an official land-use scheme; used as local planning context, not parcel-coverage proof.

searchQueries.query: Klipgat South Africa official cadastral map parcel GIS land registry North West municipality Chief Surveyor General
searchQueries.result: Anonymous point query against the official CSG-hosted Erven polygon layer returns one active parcel covering the WUP point. A safe exact-ID query returned a valid five-vertex polygon (about 299.9 m² in EPSG:32735). Esri JSON works; the same service’s GeoJSON query returns HTTP 200 with ArcGIS error 400, so the existing GeoJSON-only adapter is incompatible and no production qualification is claimed.
searchQueries.method: Separate web search followed by direct review of relevant official sources.

serviceChecks.observation: Anonymous point query at exact WUP coordinate with safe fields only found one matching Erven row (OBJECTID 5954119, PRCL_KEY GTSHT0JR065500000200000000, PRCL_TYPE E, LSTATUS R, WSTATUS C). Exact PRCL_KEY geometry query as f=json/outSR=4326 returned one polygon.
Repeated f=geojson exact-ID/point requests return ArcGIS error code 400 `Failed to execute query`; adapter currently asks for GeoJSON.

The existing adapter returned `Parcel provider is unavailable (HTTP 400)` on the exact public PRCL_KEY; transport format is the GeoJSON output the service rejects. No grid or full source qualification was run.

geometryEvidence.wireFormat: Native Esri JSON straight rings; no geometry repair.

rootNativeFormatReview.curveHandling: returnTrueCurves=true is requested; curveRings are rejected rather than flattened.
rootNativeFormatReview.statusInterpretation: R/C/E observed in all sampled rows; no lifecycle filter inferred.
